# MCP server setup — Znalica

This file was generated at delivery from the packet's server definitions (`servers.yaml`), so it is a
snapshot: `verified:` dates and commands can go stale, and a newer packet version may know better.
Re-running the delivery refreshes it. It carries setup **procedure** only — never an endpoint or a credential.
`.mcp.json` says which servers this project runs; this file says how to stand one up.

A `key_overridable` server may run in this project under a different key — check `.mcp.json`; it is the same server.

## This file is read by both tools

- **The committed `.mcp.json` is read by BOTH Claude Code and Copilot CLI, and their stdio schemas overlap
  without coinciding. Keep every stdio entry to `command` + `args`.**
- **Do not add `"type": "local"`.** Copilot's documentation uses it for `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`, but
  Claude Code rejects the value and skips the server (`Skipped — unknown MCP server type "local"`), removing
  its tools from the session with no in-session error. Omit `type` on stdio entries.
- **`copilot mcp list` prints `(local)` for a correct stdio entry** — that is Copilot's name for the stdio
  transport, not the `type` value above. Answer the question by opening `.mcp.json`, never off the listing, and
  never add `"type": "local"` to make the two agree.
- **Tool-specific options go in that tool's own config** — `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` for Copilot, or
  `claude mcp add --scope user|local` for Claude — never in the shared file.
- **One measured exception: `"alwaysLoad": true`.** It makes Claude Code (2.1.121 or later) load a server's tools
  at session start; Copilot CLI loads the file unchanged. Leave it in. Copilot's counterpart, `deferTools`, is
  not safe here: given a value it does not accept, Copilot skips that server and says so only in its debug log.
- **Copilot precondition: the project folder must be listed in `trustedFolders` in `~/.copilot/config.json`.**
  Untrusted, Copilot skips the workspace `.mcp.json` entirely, with no error at the default log level, while
  user-level servers keep loading. `copilot mcp list` is not the check. Open `~/.copilot/config.json` (it is JSONC,
  read it as text) and look for this project's path. **After renaming or moving the folder, add the new path.**
- **Claude Code binds MCP at launch.** Any change here needs a full CLI restart (for a VS Code–integrated
  session, shut VS Code down so it relaunches). Copilot CLI 1.0.93 or later applies an MCP change between
  turns; on an older Copilot, or when the tools are still missing on the next turn, restart it too.

## knowledge

- **Status in this project:** enabled by the `knowledge_base` option — routed **personal**: it is not in
  `.mcp.json`; each developer registers it in their own MCP config (`claude mcp add --transport http --scope
  local knowledge <url>` for Claude — `claude mcp add-json` to include `"alwaysLoad": true` — and
  `copilot mcp add --transport http knowledge <url>` for Copilot). Ask your knowledge-server admin for the address.
- **Who gets which tools:** every agent. The read-only agents (code-reviewer, design-reviewer, reader) get only
  the read tools `search_knowledge`, `get_article`, `list_articles`, `get_research`, `get_teachable_moment`;
  the others get the whole server. Wire it by hand the same way.
- **Always loaded:** the packet marks this server always loaded — when its entry is in `.mcp.json` it carries
  `"alwaysLoad": true` unless that was declined at delivery, so Claude Code 2.1.121 or later loads its tools at
  session start; that costs context in every session and startup waits for the server, up to 5 seconds. A
  personal registration needs the key added with `claude mcp add-json`.
- No local install: it is an HTTP server. The endpoint must be reachable before first use.
- Notes: the default key is `knowledge`; the runner supplies the URL and may rename the key.

## serena

- **Status:** enabled by the `code_navigation_mcp` option. Verified 2026-10-01.
- **Reuse, don't duplicate:** if you already run a server named `serena` (or `serena-*`) in your own MCP config,
  reuse that existing install — do not add a second.
- **Preflight:** runtime `uv`; check `serena --version` — if it succeeds, Serena is installed: skip the install.
  Install: Install uv (https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), then: `uv tool install serena-agent`
  (`setup_shortcut`: `serena setup claude-code` writes Claude's MCP config — not needed here, `.mcp.json` has it.)
- **To update:** `<latest>` is the version https://pypi.org/pypi/serena-agent/json returns (`info.version`).
  First run `uv tool list --show-version-specifiers`: offer the update only if `serena-agent` is listed with a
  plain version requirement or none. Then `uv tool install "serena-agent==<latest>"`. Read the changelog
  sections between the installed and the target version **whole** (not filtered by keyword — renamed config keys
  are not always called renames): https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oraios/serena/main/CHANGELOG.md
  Close other sessions using Serena first; a reinstall under another session's lock can leave none installed.
- **Per-project setup (once per clone):**
  ```bash
  serena project create . --language csharp --language markdown --language yaml --index
  serena memories initialize
  ```
  Skip it if `.serena/project.yml` already exists. `memories initialize` fails if `project create` has not run.
- **Who gets it:** developer, architect, doc-writer.
- Notes:
  - Not read-only: `rename_symbol` and `safe_delete_symbol` are reachable in every context and mode, which is why
    the reviewers do not get this server.
  - Claude Code's deferred tool loading can make agents under-use Serena's tools even when it is loaded and
    working; the agent bodies name `find_symbol` / `find_referencing_symbols` at the point of use.
  - uv resolves a compatible Python for serena-agent; add `-p <ver>` only to force one.

## al-language-server

- **Status:** not enabled — pulled in only by the `al-bc` language pack (this project is C# / Unity).
  Verified 2026-07-09.
- **Preflight:** runtime `al`; check `al --version`.
  Install: `dotnet tool install --global microsoft.dynamics.businesscentral.development.tools`
- **To update:** `<latest>` is the newest stable version listed at
  https://api.nuget.org/v3-flatcontainer/microsoft.dynamics.businesscentral.development.tools/index.json ;
  run `dotnet tool update --global microsoft.dynamics.businesscentral.development.tools`. Release notes: the
  package page only, https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.Dynamics.BusinessCentral.Development.Tools — no
  per-version notes.
- **Always loaded:** the packet marks this server always loaded (see the `knowledge` section for what that costs).
- **Who gets it:** developer only.
- Notes: `al_addproject` must register the project each session; `al_run_tests` needs a live Business Central
  connection.

## microsoft-learn

- **Status:** enabled by the `microsoft_docs_mcp` option. Verified 2026-10-18. HTTP, hosted by Microsoft; no
  local install, no key.
- **Reuse, don't duplicate:** if you already run a `microsoft-learn` server in your own config, reuse it.
- **Who gets it:** developer, architect, workflow, doc-writer.
- Notes: one search returns about 20K characters — search once, then fetch only the article needed. On Copilot
  CLI a large result can arrive as a saved temp file plus a short preview; read the file before concluding.

## context7

- **Status:** not enabled — the `library_docs_mcp` option was answered no. Verified 2026-10-18. HTTP, hosted
  by Upstash; no local install.
- **Reuse, don't duplicate:** `ctx7 setup` and Upstash's plugins register it per user as `context7` — reuse that.
- **Who would get it:** developer, architect, workflow, doc-writer.
- Notes: keys are per person — with a key, register your own `context7` in user-level config and commit nothing.
  Never run `ctx7 setup` in this project (it writes a literal key and a `type: stdio` entry). Without a key the
  free limit is small.

## graphify

- **Status:** enabled by the `code_graph_mcp` option. Verified 2026-10-18.
- **Reuse, don't duplicate:** if you already run a `graphify` server in your own config, reuse it.
- **Preflight:** runtime `uv`. Install uv (https://docs.astral.sh/uv/); `uvx` then fetches the pinned graphify
  on first use — nothing else to install.
- **Per-project setup (once per clone, and after large changes):**
  ```bash
  uvx --from "graphifyy[mcp]==0.9.92" graphify update .
  ```
  Skip it if `graphify-out/graph.json` already exists. `graphify-out/` is git-ignored; each clone builds its own.
- **Who gets which tools:** developer, architect, doc-writer, code-reviewer, design-reviewer, reader — the seven
  graph tools only (`query_graph`, `get_node`, `get_neighbors`, `get_community`, `god_nodes`, `graph_stats`,
  `shortest_path`), granted per tool, never server-wide. Its three pull-request tools stay with the main session.
- Notes: a graph older than the code cannot show the newest callers — rebuild after edits. It resolves names,
  it is not a type checker.
